concepts.why: The presence of papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium and mucin-containing goblet cells, without cytologic atypia or atypical mitotic figures, is consistent with inverted papilloma.

The exophytic, verrucous, skin-colored plaque with papillary fronds and nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium could be suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma, although the absence of cytologic atypia and atypical mitotic figures makes this less likely.
The verrucous appearance of the plaque and the presence of nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium could be consistent with verrucous carcinoma.
The presence of papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium and mucin-containing goblet cells is consistent with nasal papilloma.
The presence of nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium could be suggestive of squamous hyperplasia, although this would not typically present as a mass.
The presence of nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium and the absence of cytologic atypia could be consistent with reactive epithelial hyperplasia.

rationales.F01: The presence of a mass in the right nostril is more typical of inverted papilloma and nasal papilloma.
rationales.F02: Bleeding with minimal trauma is a common feature of several nasal lesions, including inverted papilloma, squamous cell carcinoma, and verrucous carcinoma.
rationales.F06: The description of the lesion as exophytic, verrucous, and skin-colored is highly suggestive of inverted papilloma, nasal papilloma, and verrucous carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The presence of papillary fronds with slender fibrovascular cores lined by nonkeratinizing squamous epithelium is characteristic of inverted papilloma.
rationales.F09: The absence of cytologic atypia and atypical mitotic figures rules out squamous cell carcinoma and suggests a more benign lesion such as inverted papilloma or nasal papilloma.
